overview: Black plays ...d6 and ...Nd7 and keeps the options of ...e5 (a Philidor Hanham set-up) or ...g6 and ...Ngf6 (a Pirc or Modern set-up). White takes space with Nc3 and Nf3, perhaps f4 or Bc4, and Black waits to strike with ...e5 or ...c5. I am not certain of the theory here, so this is reasoned from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, Nf3 and Be2 or Bc4 and keep the e4-d4 centre, perhaps with f4.
Use space against the cramped Black pieces.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...e5 and ...Ngf6 for a Philidor-style solid position.
Or ...g6, ...Bg7 and ...Ngf6 for a Pirc-type fianchetto, striking with ...c5 or ...e5.

typical_structures.structure: Philidor Hanham: Black's d6-e5 pawns and a knight on d7 against White's centre.

character.notes: Passive, hard-to-break Black set-up in the Philidor style; slow play.

structure.notes: White's centre is attacked by ...e5 or ...c5 later; the tension is undecided, so flexible.

approach.notes: Rarely played by strong players; the Rat family is a surprise choice.

level.notes: Simple plans, but the passive position needs patience.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Nc3 g6 or 3...Ngf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nd7 3. Nc3 Ngf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black switches to a Pirc-like set-up and then ...e5 or ...g6.

character.reason: A compact Philidor-style set-up that is hard to break down but passive.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided until Black commits to ...e5 or ...g6.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom use the Rat set-ups.

level.reason: Few lines to memorise but a cramped game to handle.

plans.reason: White's space against Black's cramped bishop on c8.
